{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Services Agreement (Contractor Engagement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of the Contractor services agreement — key issues and redlines

---

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the agreement. The commercial architecture is broadly acceptable to us: the engagement is task-by-task under Statements of Work with no exclusivity, no minimum commitments, no most-favoured-nation obligation, no non-compete, no auto-renewal mechanic, no audit rights running against us, and no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us on termination. Those points require no redlining.

Our concerns are concentrated in the risk-allocation provisions. Three items are critical. First, despite its heading, § 7 contains **no indemnity language at all** — the non-infringement statement in 5(c) is a warranty, not a defence obligation — so we have inserted the standard Contractor indemnity at 7(d). Second, the liability cap is measured by fees under the individual Statement of Work rather than 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, and the sole carve-out is a broken cross-reference to "Paragraph 9" (the Independent Contractor clause), leaving confidentiality, data/security, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement all capped. Third, while Works vest in us for invoiced-and-paid periods, the agreement never confirms that we retain ownership of our own data and materials, and § 4(b)(ii) sweeps "records relating to the Services" into Contractor's exclusive property.

At the high level, we lack any exit from a live Statement of Work while Contractor may walk on 15 days' notice; the assignment clause has no affiliate/successor carve-out and is silent on change of control; and the embedded-IP licence does not reach our affiliates or contractors. We have also added a conformity warranty and remedy (currently absent), transition assistance and data return/deletion obligations (currently absent), a New York governing law and venue in place of Arizona law and mandatory arbitration, a general-advertising carve-out to the non-solicit, and cyber liability cover.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Insert Contractor indemnity for IP, legal breach, data incidents and misconduct, with notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a narrow reverse indemnity from us. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | Add Company ownership of Company data and materials; confirm no transfer of our IP or data to Contractor and no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Make the cap mutual on a 12-month fee basis with standard uncapped carve-outs; exclude our payment obligations from the cap. Mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 7(b) is acceptable. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Company; confirm a change of control of Company is not an assignment and gives Contractor no termination or re-pricing right. |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 Termination | Add a 30-day Company convenience right covering any Statement of Work with pro-rata refund and no penalty; move Contractor's convenience right to 90 days between engagements. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | Make the embedded Contractor Information licence irrevocable and worldwide, extend to our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, and make it transferable to a successor. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | No sole-source, exclusivity or "all requirements" language; we remain free to use other suppliers. No change. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties | Compliant | § 6 Termination | On termination we pay only fees and expenses incurred or earned; no penalties, minimum termination fees or late-payment interest. § 5 allows us to withhold fees on an anti-bribery termination, in our favour. No change. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us; the only limit is a use restriction on Contractor's own proprietary materials. No change. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Replace Arizona law with New York law and set exclusive jurisdiction in the New York County courts in both places, displacing the mandatory arbitration in § 19 (no agreed seat). Delaware or California is our fallback. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 5 Contractor's Representations and Warranties and Warranty Disclaimer | Add a 90-day conformity warranty (12 months for software), workmanlike-performance and no-malicious-code warranties, and the standard repair/re-perform/refund remedy, protected from the 5(e) disclaimer. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 Termination | Insert wind-down paragraph at 6(d): six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day data return in usable format, certified deletion. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Mutual, 12-month, scope-limited non-solicit meets our fallback; add the standard general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-out so ordinary recruitment is not captured. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No audit, inspection or verification rights against us and no Contractor right of access to our systems. No change. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No most-favoured-nation or best-terms obligation running against us. Separately note that Contractor may change rates on 30 days' notice — a commercial point. No change. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | Time-and-materials under individual SOWs; no minimum purchase, retainer floor, take-or-pay, shortfall mechanic or volume cap. No change. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | Evergreen until terminated; no automatic renewal term, non-renewal notice window or renewal uplift mechanic (rate changes handled under § 3(b)). No change. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Raise E&O to USD 2M, add a USD 2M CGL aggregate, and add cyber/privacy liability cover (USD 5M preferred, USD 2M fallback) given Contractor handles our Confidential Information and may access our systems. |

---

## Walk-away items

We should not sign without resolution of the three critical findings:

1. **Contractor indemnity (§ 7 — missing).** We have no defence obligation for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data incidents or misconduct. A warranty alone does not substitute.
2. **Liability cap and carve-outs (§ 7).** A cap set at fees under a single Statement of Work — potentially a very small amount — with no carve-outs for confidentiality, data/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement is not an allocation we can accept. The broken cross-reference to "Paragraph 9" must also be corrected.
3. **Ownership of our data and materials (§ 4).** § 4(b)(ii) sweeping "records relating to the Services" into Contractor's exclusive property, with no express retention of our own IP and data, is unacceptable.

We would also treat the combination of no Company exit from a live Statement of Work with a 15-day Contractor walk-away right (§ 6) as close to a walk-away if Contractor refuses movement.

---

## Next steps

1. Send the marked-up agreement with the redlines described above, leading on the three critical items in §§ 4 and 7.
2. Flag to Contractor's counsel that § 7's heading promises an indemnity the clause does not contain, and that the carve-out cross-reference to "Paragraph 9" points to the Independent Contractor clause — both are likely drafting errors and should be uncontroversial to fix.
3. Offer our stated fallbacks where helpful: Delaware or California law if New York is resisted (finding 10), and USD 2M cyber cover if USD 5M is resisted (finding 18).
4. Refer the § 3(b) right to change rates on 30 days' notice to the business team as a commercial, not legal, point.
5. Confirm with the business the required duration and scope of post-termination transition assistance so the 6(d) wind-down language matches operational need.
6. Circulate the insurance requirements to risk management for confirmation before we exchange drafts."}
